ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Angular steering of refusal in a single plane of the residual stream on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
PROPOSAL: Estimate a refusal direction in one of the middle layers, layer 14, of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct from the difference of mean activations on 256 harmful and 256 harmless instructions, then rotate activations inside the plane spanned by that direction and the first principal component of the harmless set, leaving the orthogonal complement untouched. The rotation angle is the only control parameter and does not depend on activation norms. Move the angle in steps of 30 degrees over the full circle on 100 held-out harmful prompts from AdvBench and 100 harmless prompts from Alpaca, and record refusal rate by keyword match and by a judge model, and perplexity on 500 WikiText passages.
CONTROLS: Unsteered model, activation addition with a coefficient tuned on a validation split, directional ablation of the same direction, and rotation in a random plane of equal dimension; three seeds for the random plane.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Refusal rate should vary smoothly with the angle, from near total at zero to near zero at 180 degrees, with perplexity within 3 percent of baseline. It could fail if the plane is dominated by norm effects so that partial angles give erratic behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-by-layer study of plane rotation for refusal control in open models
PROPOSAL: Build the refusal direction from mean activation differences over 128 harmful and 128 harmless instructions, then rotate activations in the plane formed by that direction and the leading principal component of harmless activations. Place the rotation at layers 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 in turn for Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, and likewise for two smaller open models. Test on 100 harmful prompts from AdvBench and 100 harmless prompts from Alpaca, with angles in steps of 15 degrees, recording refusal by keyword and by a judge model, and perplexity on WikiText. Report the angle at which refusal falls below half for each layer, with bootstrap intervals over prompts.
CONTROLS: Unsteered model, activation addition with a coefficient tuned on a validation split, directional ablation of the same direction, and rotation in a random plane of equal dimension; three seeds for the random plane.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Refusal rate should vary smoothly with the angle, from near total at zero to near zero at 180 degrees, at middle layers, with perplexity close to baseline. It could fail if the plane is dominated by norm effects so that partial angles give erratic behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Strength scans of norm-invariant steering against activation addition on Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
PROPOSAL: Compare a norm-invariant rotation edit with activation addition as the control strength varies, on Qwen2.5 7B Instruct. For each method, choose the target layer by validation refusal gain on 200 prompts, then evaluate on 300 harmful prompts from HarmBench and 300 harmless prompts from OR-Bench at 9 strengths. Track refusal rate, MMLU accuracy on 1000 questions, perplexity on 500 WikiText passages and a fluency score by a judge model, and plot each against strength to locate where degradation begins for either method.
CONTROLS: Activation addition with a raw coefficient, activation addition with a coefficient scaled by the layer's mean activation norm, directional ablation, and the unsteered model; five seeds for the judge sampling temperature.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The rotation edit should keep MMLU and perplexity flat over the whole range while addition degrades them beyond a layer-dependent strength. It could fail if the rotation gives a narrower range of refusal rates than addition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does one control parameter work at every depth? Rotation and addition on the Qwen2.5 family
PROPOSAL: Ask whether a single strength setting transfers between layers. On Qwen2.5 7B Instruct, apply a norm-invariant rotation and activation addition at layers 6, 14 and 22, scoring 300 harmful prompts from HarmBench and 300 harmless prompts from OR-Bench at 9 strengths. Carry the study to smaller and bigger siblings in the family. Track refusal rate, MMLU accuracy on 1000 questions, perplexity on WikiText and a fluency score by a judge model, and plot each against strength for each depth and model size.
CONTROLS: Activation addition with a raw coefficient, activation addition with a coefficient scaled by the layer's mean activation norm, directional ablation and the unsteered model; five seeds for the judge sampling temperature.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The rotation edit should keep MMLU and perplexity flat over the whole range while addition degrades them beyond a layer-dependent strength. It could fail if the rotation gives a narrower range of refusal rates than addition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing rotation, addition and ablation of the refusal feature on Gemma 2 9B
PROPOSAL: On Gemma 2 9B instruction-tuned, extract refusal directions at every fourth layer using 512 contrastive pairs, and evaluate three edits at each layer: rotation by a fixed angle, addition with a tuned coefficient, and directional ablation. Test on 400 harmful prompts from JailbreakBench plus 400 harmless prompts from Alpaca, scoring refusal with a judge model and measuring general ability on MMLU, GSM8K and TruthfulQA. Report, per layer, the tradeoff curve between refusal change and loss in general ability, and the layer at which each edit gives the best tradeoff.
CONTROLS: Unedited model, random-direction edits of matched norm, edits using a direction estimated from a different set of 512 pairs, and a prompt-based refusal instruction; two seeds for the random directions.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Rotation should give the best tradeoff at intermediate layers and degrade least on GSM8K. It could fail if the direction estimated at one layer transfers poorly and all edits give similar tradeoffs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Survey of refusal edits on Gemma 2 9B with directions from varied contrastive data
PROPOSAL: Extract refusal directions on Gemma 2 9B instruction-tuned at layers 8, 16 and 24 from contrastive pairs drawn from different sources, and apply rotation, addition and directional ablation at graded strengths. Test on 400 harmful prompts from JailbreakBench and 400 harmless prompts from Alpaca, scoring refusal with a judge model and measuring general ability on MMLU, GSM8K, TruthfulQA, HellaSwag, ARC and WinoGrande. Report the tradeoff curve between refusal change and loss in general ability for each edit and each source.
CONTROLS: Unedited model, random-direction edits of matched norm and a prompt-based refusal instruction; two seeds for the random directions.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Rotation should give the best tradeoff at intermediate layers and degrade least on GSM8K. It could fail if the direction estimated from one source transfers poorly and all edits give similar tradeoffs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Testing the commutation of rotation edits with RMS normalization at inference time
PROPOSAL: Check on Llama 3.2 1B that a rotation inside a two-dimensional plane followed by RMS normalization gives the same direction as normalization followed by the rotation, up to a scalar, and measure where this fails numerically. Collect residual-stream activations at layers 4, 8 and 12 on 1000 WikiText passages, apply rotations by 15 angles, and calculate the angle between the two orderings and the relative norm change. Contrast with activation addition at coefficients matched on the post-normalization norm.
CONTROLS: A random orthogonal map of the same plane, a scaling edit in place of rotation, and a float32 reference calculation against bfloat16.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Both orderings should agree to within numerical precision, while addition should show a norm-dependent angle error growing with depth. It could fail if the epsilon term inside normalization produces an offset visible at small norms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Numerical audit of rotation edits and RMS normalization in three number formats
PROPOSAL: Verify on Llama 3.2 1B that a planar rotation followed by RMS normalization points the same way as normalization followed by the rotation, and map where the two orderings part ways. Gather residual-stream activations at seven evenly spaced layers on passages from WikiText, C4 and GitHub code, apply rotations by 30 angles in float32, float16 and bfloat16, and calculate the angle between the orderings and the relative norm change at each token position.
CONTROLS: A random orthogonal map of the same plane, a scaling edit in place of rotation, and a float32 reference calculation against the lower precisions.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Both orderings should agree to within numerical precision, with errors growing slowly with depth in lower precisions. It could fail if the epsilon term inside normalization produces an offset visible at small norms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuous emotion control of generated stories by plane rotation
PROPOSAL: Estimate directions for joy, anger and sadness from the difference of mean activations on 300 short emotional passages versus neutral ones, and rotate activations toward each direction inside a two-dimensional plane at layer 16 of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. Generate 5 stories of 200 tokens for each of 100 neutral story openings at 7 angles. Score emotion intensity with a fine-tuned classifier and with a judge model, and measure coherence by perplexity under the unsteered model and lexical diversity.
CONTROLS: Activation addition tuned on a validation split, prompt-based emotion instructions, unsteered generation, and rotation toward a random direction; two seeds for the sampling.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Emotion intensity should grow monotonically with angle until about 90 degrees with stable coherence. It could fail if the three emotions share one valence direction and rotations cannot separate them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An emotion dial for generated text: five emotions, three model families
PROPOSAL: Build directions for joy, anger, sadness, fear and surprise from mean activation differences between emotional and neutral passages, and turn activations toward each inside a two-dimensional plane. Story generation starts from neutral openings, with a spread of angles and a chosen layer on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B. Score emotion intensity with a fine-tuned classifier and a judge model, and measure coherence by perplexity and lexical diversity.
CONTROLS: Activation addition tuned on a validation split, prompt-based emotion instructions, unsteered generation, and rotation toward a random direction; two seeds per model.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Emotion intensity should grow monotonically with angle until about 90 degrees with stable coherence. It could fail if the emotions share one valence direction and rotations cannot separate them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leaving unrelated features untouched: a two-dimensional edit against a full-space edit
PROPOSAL: Test whether restricting the edit to a two-dimensional plane protects unrelated features better than editing the full activation space. On Llama 3.1 8B Instruct at layer 14, apply a refusal edit of matched effect either in the plane or in the full space, then train linear probes on frozen activations for sentiment, topic, toxicity, language identity and part of speech using 20000 labeled sentences, and measure probe accuracy before and after the edit. Evaluate MMLU and perplexity under both edits.
CONTROLS: Probe accuracy under random-plane edits, under addition of matched norm, and on the unedited model; probes retrained from scratch with three seeds, and a held-out probe family.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The planar edit should lower probe accuracy by under one point while full-space edits lower it by several. It could fail if the chosen plane overlaps strongly with sentiment or toxicity directions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Side effects of steering on probed features over depth and probe families
PROPOSAL: Compare planar rotation with whole-space editing for collateral damage. On Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, apply a refusal edit of matched effect at five evenly spaced layers, then train linear probes on frozen activations for sentiment, topic, toxicity, language identity, part of speech, tense, negation and named entities, and measure probe accuracy before and after the edit at 6 angles. Report MMLU and perplexity under both kinds of edit.
CONTROLS: Probe accuracy under random-plane edits, under addition of matched norm, and on the unedited model; probes retrained from scratch with three seeds.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The planar edit should lower probe accuracy by under one point while full-space edits lower it by several. It could fail if the chosen plane overlaps strongly with sentiment or toxicity directions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reliability of refusal steering over model families and sizes
PROPOSAL: Evaluate one rotation recipe on five families at two sizes each, a small and a big member of Llama 3.1, Qwen2.5, Gemma 2, Mistral and OLMo 2. In each model pick the layer by validation gain on 200 prompts, move the angle in steps of 30 degrees, and score refusal on 300 harmful prompts from HarmBench and over-refusal on 300 benign prompts from XSTest. Measure MMLU accuracy and perplexity for retention, and fit the refusal curve with a logistic function of the angle for each model.
CONTROLS: Activation addition and directional ablation tuned on the same validation split for each model, the unsteered model, and a random-plane rotation; two seeds for the random plane.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The logistic fit should give a similar midpoint angle within each family and a shift between families. It could fail if larger models need a different layer fraction so that the recipe breaks without tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A recipe for refusal control tested under many data sources and plane constructions
PROPOSAL: Take Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 and Gemma 2, and test the rotation recipe under 5 sources of contrastive pairs and 4 ways of choosing the second axis of the plane. Pick the layer by validation gain on 200 prompts, sweep the angle in steps of 15 degrees, and score refusal on 300 harmful prompts from HarmBench and over-refusal on 300 benign prompts from XSTest. Add MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC and perplexity to measure retention, and fit a logistic curve of refusal against the angle for each combination.
CONTROLS: Activation addition and directional ablation tuned on the same validation split for each model, the unsteered model and a random-plane rotation; two seeds for the random plane.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The logistic fit should give a similar midpoint angle within each family and a shift between families. It could fail if the data source changes the direction enough that the recipe breaks without tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-grained response curve of refusal probability to steering angle
PROPOSAL: Characterize how behavior changes as the angle varies continuously, using one of the middle layers, layer 14, of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. At angles over the full circle in steps of 5, calculate for 400 harmful prompts the probability of the first response token being a refusal marker, and the first-token entropy; generate full responses at a dozen chosen angles and classify them as refusal, partial compliance or compliance with a judge model. Fit a sigmoid to the refusal probability and locate the angle range where partial compliance occurs.
CONTROLS: Curves from activation addition at 20 coefficients, curves from ablation scaled between zero and one, and the unsteered model; three seeds for sampled responses.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: The refusal probability should follow a sigmoid in the angle with a narrow transition region holding most partial compliance. It could fail if first-token probabilities and full responses disagree about where the transition lies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mapping the transition between refusing and complying on Mistral 7B Instruct by prompt category
PROPOSAL: Follow how Mistral 7B Instruct moves from refusing to complying as the steering angle turns, with the rotation placed at three middle layers. For 400 harmful prompts in four HarmBench categories, measure the probability that the first response token is a refusal marker and its entropy over a dense grid of angles, then generate 5 full responses per prompt at 12 angles and label them refusal, partial compliance or compliance with a judge model. Fit a sigmoid to each category and compare where the partial-compliance band falls.
CONTROLS: Curves from activation addition at 20 coefficients, curves from ablation scaled between zero and one, and the unsteered model; three seeds for sampled responses.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: The refusal probability should follow a sigmoid in the angle with a narrow transition region holding most partial compliance, with category shifts of modest size. It could fail if first-token probabilities and full responses disagree about where the transition lies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Inverting refusal: pushing against the feature direction on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
PROPOSAL: Test whether moving activations to the opposite side of the refusal direction induces compliance beyond what ablation gives. On Llama 3.1 8B Instruct at layer 14, rotate by angles from 120 to 240 degrees in steps of 20 on 200 harmful prompts from AdvBench, and measure the compliance rate with a judge model, the harmfulness of completions, and the rate of refusing benign requests from XSTest at the same angles. Report perplexity on 300 WikiText passages to check coherence.
CONTROLS: Directional ablation of the refusal direction, activation addition with a negative coefficient, and the unsteered model; two seeds for generation sampling.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Angles near 180 degrees should give higher compliance than ablation with unchanged benign behavior. It could fail if inversion produces incoherent text rather than compliance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Past ablation in three families: does opposing the refusal feature induce compliance?
PROPOSAL: Probe whether crossing to the negative side of the refusal direction yields more compliance than removing the feature. Use Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B at three middle layers, with rotations from 120 to 240 degrees in steps of 20 on 200 harmful AdvBench prompts. Measure compliance by a judge model, harmfulness of completions, over-refusal on XSTest at matching angles, and coherence through perplexity on 300 WikiText passages, MMLU and GSM8K.
CONTROLS: Directional ablation of the refusal direction, activation addition with a negative coefficient, and the unsteered model; two seeds for generation sampling.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Angles near 180 degrees should give higher compliance than ablation with unchanged benign behavior. It could fail if inversion produces incoherent text rather than compliance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Selective steering versus conditional steering for refusal on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
PROPOSAL: Compare rotation-based control with a conditional method that applies the edit only when a condition vector fires. On Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, edit only harmful-topic prompts for the compliance direction, and measure whether harmless prompts keep the same responses. Use 300 harmful prompts from HarmBench and 600 harmless prompts from Alpaca and OR-Bench; report refusal change, exact-match agreement of harmless responses with the unsteered model, MMLU accuracy and perplexity. Test conditions from a linear probe on the layers around layer 12 and from the same refusal direction.
CONTROLS: Conditional activation addition with the published thresholds, unconditional rotation, unconditional addition, and a random-condition control; three seeds for the random condition.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Conditional rotation should keep harmless responses nearly unchanged while giving the same refusal change as unconditional rotation. It could fail if the condition fires on benign prompts that resemble harmful ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Thresholds and condition layers for gated rotation edits in three model families
PROPOSAL: Gate a rotation edit by a condition vector and study how its threshold and the layer of the condition shape side effects. For Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B, apply the edit to harmful-topic prompts and check that harmless ones keep their responses. Over 6 thresholds and 4 condition layers, report refusal change on HarmBench prompts, exact-match agreement of harmless responses with the unsteered model across Alpaca and OR-Bench, MMLU accuracy and perplexity, with conditions from a linear probe or from the refusal direction.
CONTROLS: Conditional activation addition with the published thresholds, unconditional rotation, unconditional addition and a random-condition control; three seeds for the random condition.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Conditional rotation should keep harmless responses nearly unchanged while giving the same refusal change as unconditional rotation. It could fail if the condition fires on benign prompts that resemble harmful ones.
